manufacturer_data.description: Company id app-confirmed: the app's broadcast parser requires the bytes 88 EC in the manufacturer-specific AD structure, and reads goodsType as 2 bytes big-endian immediately after them (AD payload offsets 3-4 in the layout that carries a leading broadcast-version byte, 2-3 in the one that does not). That version byte is why hosts may report company 0x88XX instead of 0xEC88 — match the 88 EC bytes at payload offset 0 or 1. Plug goodsTypes: 43=single, 50 & 307=dual, 90=triple. Last byte = on/off state (0x00/0x01; dual: bit0=right, bit1=left).

The app's broadcast parser requires the bytes 88 EC in the manufacturer-specific AD structure (= company 0xEC88 / 60552 when they lead the payload). A leading broadcast-version byte shifts them to payload offset 1, making host stacks report 0x88XX instead — 0x8802, 0x8803 and 0x8843 are the values seen on Govee lights (2026-08-22), listed here because the broadcast layout is shared across Govee families, not because they were observed on a plug. Match on the bytes at payload offset 0 or 1, not on the parsed company id. A previous revision of this spec claimed 63678, which appears in no source.

device.name: Govee H5080 Smart Plug
device.notes:
WiFi + BLE smart plug family from Govee. Local BLE control uses the classic Govee 20-byte binary packet — [2-byte command][17-byte payload][1-byte XOR checksum] — wire-verified (egold555 H5080.md, virtuald/govee-ble-plugs plugs.py), NOT IoT-style JSON ("turn"/"state" are keys of the app's internal IoT abstraction, not what goes on the wire). The plug also has a 2.4 GHz WiFi radio (FCC 2AQA6-H5080 lists 2412-2462 MHz; manual spec panel "IEEE 802.11 b/g/n, 2.4GHz") and a cloud binding; BLE local control works without WiFi or cloud.
Family members: - H5080: single plug (goodsType=43) - H5081: single plug variant (retail SKU, FCC 2AQA6-H5081; absent
  from the APK's h5080 package — family membership unproven)
- H5082: dual plug (goodsType=50; RE'd — right=port0, left=port1) - H5083: dual plug - H5085: Smart Plug Pro, single plug with Matter support - H5086: Smart Plug Pro Energy Monitoring (AA00 power metrics) - H5089: triple plug (goodsType=90) - H5160: triple plug variant - H5161: triple v2 (goodsTypes seen in app: 43 single, 50 & 307 dual,
  90 triple)

COMMAND MAP (20-byte packets written to …2b11; responses echo the command id and arrive on …2b10): - AA01: get state - AA06 / AA20 / AA21: get firmware version (ASCII in payload) - AA07: get hardware version - AA00: power metrics (H5086 → EE19 response: seconds-powered-on,
  Wh ×0.1, voltage ×0.01 V, current ×0.01 A, power ×0.01 W,
  power factor %)
- AAB1: get auth key (valid 16-byte key only while the physical
  button is pressed; otherwise a random decoy)
- 33B2 <16-byte key>: authenticate this connection - 3301 <byte>: set on/off. Single-plug H5080: 0xFF on / 0xF0 off
  (all-ports selector — what the app's switch controller emits when
  it addresses every port at once).
The device also sends unsolicited 3301 state notifications on physical-button presses, and the last manufacturer-data byte of the advertisement carries state (0x00/0x01; dual: bit0=right, bit1=left).
On/off byte encoding (from the app's switch controller): - bits 0-3: on-state per port (1=port0, 2=port1, 4=port2, 15=all) - bits 4-7: port selector (0x10=port0, 0x20=port1, 0x40=port2, 0xF0=all) e.g. 0x11 = port 0 on (0x10|0x01), 0x22 = port 1 on (0x20|0x02), 0x10 = port 0 off. Port-specific bytes are for multi-plug units; the single H5080 is driven with the all-ports 0xFF/0xF0 form.
FIRMWARE LANDSCAPE: versions seen are 1.00.21 and 1.02.00 (RE captures) and 1.00.22 in the wild (2025-12 user report); the app treats fw <= 1.00.08 as an "old H5080" with reduced features (a dedicated capability check in its feature gating). OTA is in-app only — no public firmware downloads.
PHYSICAL: 15 A / 1800 W max, ETL + FCC certified (FCC-filed manual spec panel).
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for wire format, UUIDs, command bytes, and the auth flow — all wire-verified by two independent implementations (egold555 Govee-Reverse-Engineering H5080.md @ fe0cd60; virtuald/ govee-ble-plugs plugs.py @ 2cf65db). The manufacturer company_id is app-confirmed (0xEC88 = 60552; recorded in the identification and discovery blocks). Two items still want a single nRF capture: whether the 128-bit service UUID is in the ADV packet, and whether a plug uses the leading-version-byte broadcast layout that makes hosts report 0x88XX — that layout is confirmed on Govee lights, not on a plug.

issued_to_client: Static 16-byte BLE auth key (AAB1, gated by physical button press)
credentials.notes: No WiFi passphrase crosses the BLE control link. App-layer token auth gates switching: unauthenticated 3301 commands are ignored, and key issuance (AAB1) requires a physical button press — an RF-only attacker cannot toggle the outlet without the key. Residual risks: the key is static, sent in cleartext (sniffable during a legitimate session), and cannot be rotated. Ecosystem advisory: CVE-2025-10910 (CERT Polska, 2025-12) — Govee cloud device-binding flaw (CWE-639) enabling account takeover of online devices; relevant because this plug IS cloud-connected. Server-side fixes + OTA patches were deployed by Govee.
stored_on_device: WiFi credentials (2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n; app-driven onboarding, separate from the BLE control path)

factory_reset.effect: Not established — no source covers a reset procedure. The plug is NOT stateless: it holds WiFi credentials, a cloud binding, and the static BLE auth key, so a real reset would have something to clear. Cutting mains power is the only confirmed state change and is not known to clear anything.

methods.description: Scan (local-name prefix ihoment_H5080_), connect, subscribe to notify char …2b10, fetch the auth key with AAB1 while the physical button is pressed, authenticate with 33B2, then write 20-byte binary commands to …2b11.

steps.action: Power the plug and scan for BLE advertisements (name prefix ihoment_H5080_).
Press and hold the physical button on the plug.
Send AAB1 while the button is held to read the 16-byte auth key; store it.
Authenticate the connection with 33B2 <key>, then write control commands (e.g. 3301).

setup.notes: No BLE bonding/pairing, but there IS an application-layer token auth: AAB1 returns the device's static 16-byte key only while the physical button is being pressed, and each connection must authenticate with 33B2 <key> — unauthenticated 3301 commands are silently ignored. First-time key retrieval therefore needs physical access; after that the key can be reused (it is static and never rotatable). Device advertises on power-up.

rejoin.notes: The plug accepts one BLE client at a time; any client holding the auth key can reconnect and re-authenticate with 33B2 once the previous client disconnects. WiFi/cloud state is unaffected by BLE client changes.

characteristics.name: State Notify
characteristics.notes: Response/notification channel (RECV char in govee-ble-plugs plugs.py). Carries command responses (command id echoed) and unsolicited 3301 state notifications on physical-button presses.

authenticate.description: 33B2 <16-byte key>: authenticate this connection. Required before 3301 is honored; the app sends it immediately before every switch command. Full frame: 33 B2 <16 key bytes> 00 <xor>.

packet_layout.2: key, 16 bytes as read back from AAB1, bytes 2 to 17

checksum.description: XOR of the preceding 19 frame bytes; encoder-filled, never a control.

key.description: The static 16-byte device key read with AAB1 while the physical button is held. Plugs use a 16-byte key; the Govee light families use an 8-byte one on the same AAB1/33B2 mechanism.

get_auth_key.description: AAB1: read the static 16-byte auth key. Only returns the valid key (payload[0]=0x01) while the physical button is pressed; otherwise a random decoy (payload[0]=0x00).

get_firmware_version.description: Get firmware version as ASCII in the payload (AA06 / AA20 / AA21 all seen on the wire).

get_power_metrics.description: H5086 only: AA00 → EE19 response decoding to seconds-powered-on, accumulated Wh (×0.1), voltage (×0.01 V), current (×0.01 A), power (×0.01 W), power factor (%).

get_state.description: Query on/off state (AA01). Response echoes AA01 on …2b10; state is also in the advertisement manufacturer-data last byte.

turn_off.description: Turn outlet off (single-plug H5080, all-ports selector). Full frame: 33 01 f0 00×16 c2.

turn_on.description: Turn outlet on (single-plug H5080, all-ports selector). Full frame: 33 01 ff 00×16 cd.

characteristics.name: Control Write
characteristics.notes:
Primary control characteristic (SEND char in plugs.py; props [read, write-without-response] per H5080.md). 20-byte binary packets; requires 33B2 authentication first — unauthenticated 3301 commands are ignored. The on/off byte encodes port + state (from the app's switch controller): bits 0-3 on-state per port (1=port0, 2=port1, 4=port2, 15=all), bits 4-7 port selector (0x10=port0, 0x20=port1, 0x40=port2, 0xF0=all). Example: byte 0x11 = port 0 on (0x10 | 0x01)
         byte 0x22 = port 1 on (0x20 | 0x02)
         byte 0x10 = port 0 off (0x10 | 0x00)
The single-plug H5080 is driven with the all-ports form: 0xFF on / 0xF0 off.

services.name: Govee H5080 Plug Service
services.notes: All commands are classic Govee 20-byte binary packets: [2-byte command][17-byte payload, zero-padded][1-byte XOR checksum of bytes 0-18]. Write to …2b11; responses (echoing the command id) and unsolicited state notifications arrive on …2b10.
